title: Ensemble runner: runner.yaml
description: This computer's runner: a worker that runs the tasks its hub keeps for the git repositories of its workspace with the helper teams in its teams directory, and, through the hub, may lend this computer's power to others. In ~/.config/ensemble/runner/runner.yaml; a computer runs one runner. Nothing has a default value; `hub`, `llm.hub` and a backend's `api_key_env` may be left out, which means they are not used.

name.description: Its name, which a hub knows as <owner>/<name>: letters, digits, '-', '_' or '.'.

works_for.description: owner: it works for its owner alone. hub: also on the tasks of every account whose role has `compute`, when no runner of the account's own with the agent takes them; connecting it needs `host`. It works others' tasks only with the agents of its teams that run on LLM backends, never on an agent CLI's own login or subscription, in <workspace>/.for/<account>/<project>.

workspace.description: The folder it works in, such as ~/ensemble. Each git repository directly inside it is a project, named for its folder: the runner runs the tasks the hub keeps for it, and finds a repository added later within half a minute; a task for a project it has no folder for, it clones here from the repository the task names. ~/ is the home directory; a relative path is beside runner.yaml.

hub.description: The hub server it connects to, ws:// or wss://, signed in to with `ensemble-runner login`: the tasks the hub has for you, and what it offers. Leave it out for no hub.

llm.description: The LLM backends its teams' agents run on. A team names a backend by its name alone, so a team runs on any runner that defines the backends it names. A name is unique across both groups.

hub.description: Backends other runners offer, reached through the hub: each looks like any OpenAI-compatible backend to the agents. Left out: none.

direct.description: Backends this computer calls itself, and those of them it offers through the hub.

backends.description: The key is the backend's name: letters, digits, '-', '_' or '.'. `{}` when there are none.

shares.description: The backends it offers through the hub, to the hub and to other runners: OpenAI-compatible ones only. With `works_for: owner`, to its owner's other runners and the hub; with `works_for: hub`, also to every account whose role has `compute`. They never learn its address or key. [] offers nothing.

max_shared_calls.description: The most calls of others to its shared backends at once, all of them together. The hub keeps the rest waiting for up to 10 seconds, then answers that it is busy, and the caller tries the next model of its list.

backends.description: The key is the backend's name here: letters, digits, '-', '_' or '.'.

relayed.description: A backend another runner offers, reached through the hub: OpenAI-compatible, as a runner offers no other kind.

runner.description: The runner that offers it, as the hub knows it: <owner>/<name>, such as ana/gpu-box.

backend.description: Its name in that runner's llm.direct.

llm_backend.description: How the model is reached. `type` decides which other settings there are.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key, sent as x-api-key. Keys are never written in this file.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take.

type.description: openai-compatible-api: any /chat/completions endpoint (llama-server, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, a hosted API).

base_url.description: Where the endpoint is, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1.

api_key_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the API key. Keys are never written in this file. Leave it out when the endpoint wants none.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds one request to this backend may take.
